confidence_notes: I estimated the restaurant meal, coffee and beer prices from three web searches. These used aggregated crowdsourced cost-of-living data from mid-2026, including Numbeo-based figures as of June 2026: inexpensive meal about $18, three-course meal for two about $65, cappuccino about $5.19 and domestic 0.5 L draught about $5.25. Other aggregators gave similar figures, with beer at about $6 to $6.15 and cappuccino at about $5.22 to $5.43. I put beer at the upper end because a restaurant serving usually costs more than the pub average. The cocktail and wine prices are less certain. The search found only undated bar-category averages of about $8 to $9 for cocktails and no reliable average for a glass of wine. I raised both prices for restaurant and bar menus in mid-2026 and set wine slightly below cocktails, using the usual US price gap relative to beer. The accommodation prices are my own estimates from general knowledge, without checking listings. San Antonio has very few registered hostels, so the dorm and private hostel prices are particularly uncertain. Hotel prices assume July, which is hot and moderately busy for tourism, with no major event surge.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared San Antonio with large, fairly affordable Sun Belt US cities such as Houston, Dallas and Phoenix. Its dining and drink prices are slightly below the national urban average. Hotel prices are typical for a mid-tier US tourist city, with higher rates near the River Walk and downtown.
